standard_prerequisites.name: The regular-model situation, the degree pairing, and the rank statement for recurring symmetric matrices
standard_prerequisites.statement: The situation fixes a discrete valuation ring, a smooth projective curve over its fraction field, a regular proper model and the components of the special fibre with their multiplicities; the degree pairing on combinations of components is symmetric and its value on two components is the degree of the restriction of the invertible sheaf attached to one of them to the other, which is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when the components are disjoint. The special fibre is connected and is a principal divisor on the model, so its pairing with every component vanishes, and the chapter's rank statement for symmetric recurring real matrices gives the semidefiniteness with kernel spanned by the multiplicity vector. The author's own lemmas of the chapter are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma records the formal properties of the intersection form that every later computation of the chapter uses, in particular the semidefiniteness which forces the proportionality of a combination with vanishing self-intersection to the fibre.

core_obligations: Positivity of the off-diagonal entries: for distinct components the pairing is the degree of the restriction of the invertible sheaf attached to one of them to the other, which is nonnegative, and it vanishes exactly when the components do not meet, which is the first assertion (source lines 4772-4780).
Vanishing on the fibre: the special fibre is a principal divisor on the model, so its pairing with any component vanishes, which is the second assertion (source lines 4780-4784).

Semidefiniteness and the kernel: applying the chapter's rank statement for symmetric recurring real matrices to the intersection matrix together with the multiplicity vector shows that the form is negative semidefinite with kernel exactly the multiples of the fibre, which are the remaining assertions (source lines 4784-4790).

proof_roadmap.step: Positivity of the off-diagonal pairings and their vanishing exactly on disjoint components.
The vanishing of the pairing of the fibre with every component.
Semidefiniteness and the identification of the kernel through the rank statement.
